slides.title: Programs need memory
slides.text: A variable is a named box that holds a value while the program runs. The program can read it and change it.
slides.alt: The starter program counts with a box named x: set x to 0, change x by 1. The value works, but the name says nothing.

focus.cue: This program's box is named x. It works — but says nothing.
x goes up by 1 for every gem Bolt picks up.

slides.title: Names are for people
slides.text: The computer is happy with x. The person reading your program is not. gemsLeft says exactly what the box holds.
slides.alt: The same counting program with the box named count: set count to 0 and change count by 1 read like a sentence.

focus.cue: Same program, better name: count says what it holds.
change count by 1 reads like a sentence.

slides.title: Boxes have types
slides.text: A number box counts. A flag box (a Boolean) is on or off, like hasKey. A word box holds one word from a list, like color. Pick the type that fits.
slides.alt: A flag variable in the tray: set hasKey to Off at the start, and set hasKey to On inside the if block that picks the key up.

focus.cue: hasKey is a flag box: it starts Off.
Pick up the key, and the flag flips On.
The watch strip shows the flag's value: Off, for now.

slides.title: Watch the value
slides.text: Set puts a value in. Change by adds to what is there, and a negative number takes away.
slides.alt: The watch strip reads steps = 4 after two changes: the plan set steps to 6, and each change steps by -1 brings it down.

focus.cue: Each change by -1 takes one away.
Watch the value land: steps = 4 now.

words.means: a named box that holds a value
the kind of value: a number, a flag or a word
a flag that is only true or false, on or off
add a number (or take one away) from the value

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Robo Route at Variables and finish 4 levels, so you meet the on/off flag. When the shelf offers names, pick the one a partner would understand.
slides.alt: The starter program counts with a box named x: set x to 0, change x by 1. The value works, but the name says nothing.
